newsitem.title: JAPAN: Non-bank Koei Corp says seeks special liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Non-bank Koei Corp says seeks special liquidation.

text.p: Non-bank finance firm Koei Corp, in which the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) has a stake, said on Monday that it had sought liquidation under court protection at the Tokyo District Court.
Koei said its debts as of the end of December 1996 totalled 264.1 billion yen. Koei is unlisted.

The size of the debts means that the case is Japan's largest insolvency case since the beginning of this year and the ninth largest non-bank insolvency case in Japanese corporate history, research company Teikoku Databank Ltd said in a statement.

The company lent aggressively for real estate projects in past years and, like many other firms which have been forced to seek creditor protection, has suffered from the slump in the Japanese property market. It tried to restructure its business under a five-year restructuring programme but could not improve its business, said Teikoku Databank, which specialises in insolvency data.
Koei is 55.16 percent owned by its board members and four percent owned by IBJ, a lawyer for Koei said.
The company made the court filing on Monday.

A Koei official said in late December that Koei's debts totalled 259.4 billion yen at the end of March 1996, of which 61.2 billion was in loans from the IBJ. He added that Koei's other creditors included Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, which had outstanding loans of 9.6 billion yen to Koei.
A bank official, who did not wish to be identified, said on Monday that Koei's move would have limited impact on the business of creditor banks.
"We were informed late last year that Koei would seek special liquidation so our loss from Koei's move was already covered by loan-loss provisions," the official said.
